checked_sources.source: Saha & Ramdas 2026, Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection, arXiv:2607.28322v1, Section 5.1 and Appendix C.3
checked_sources.result: Primary-source HTML verification. The universal-inference t e-process is R_{s:t}^theta = A_{s:t}{n^{-1}sum(X_i-theta)^2}^{n/2}, with a theta-independent predictive factor. It is valid uniformly over unknown Gaussian variance. Each R is convex in theta; its derivative is explicit; the all-start objective is one-dimensional convex and the minimizer lies between interval means. The source all-start implementation costs O(t log(1/epsilon_num)) per time and O(t) memory. Theorem 5.2 proves high-probability late-change delay log A/I_t using only a pure post-change start T+1 for theta near the pre-mean and the prefix start 1 for theta outside that neighborhood.

derived_results.claim: The K-grid/prefix pathwise-lower architecture extends exactly to Gaussian mean changes with unknown and unrestricted variance by replacing the closed-form quadratic pair score with an exact two-function convex minimax.
derived_results.derivation: For any retained trailing start s and prefix start 1 at time t, define V_{s,t}:=inf_theta max{R_{s:t}^theta,R_{1:t}^theta}. The full studentized detector is D_t=inf_theta sum_u R_{u:t}^theta, so D_t>=V_{s,t} pathwise. Therefore max over any retained pair set is also <=D_t, and thresholding it can only stop later than the source detector. Theorem 2.2's ARL/local false-alarm validity therefore transfers exactly, independent of numerical/statistical approximations used for the alternative-delay analysis.

derived_results.claim: Each studentized pair certificate can be evaluated from recyclable per-start sufficient state using a certified one-dimensional convex lower solver, reducing active-history cost from all t starts to O(K log t) starts.
derived_results.derivation: For an interval of length n, R^theta equals a known positive theta-independent factor times {SSE/n+(theta-xbar)^2}^{n/2}. Hence each R is convex and decreases to its interval mean then increases. The pair objective f(theta)=max{R_short(theta),R_prefix(theta)} is convex and its minimizer lies between the two interval means. Counts, sums, sums of squares and cumulative predictive log scores are exactly the per-start states already identified by the source. Moen-style K-grid recycling retains only O(K log t) starts plus the prefix. A safeguarded subgradient/bisection bracket can locate the minimizer; to preserve pathwise validity numerically, use supporting-line/interval lower envelopes and threshold only a certified lower bound on inf f. Ordinary approximate minimization is unsafe because it generally returns an upper approximation to the infimum.
derived_results.complexity_scope: With O(1) pair-function/subgradient evaluation from maintained state, active-state update/storage is O(K log t). Certified scalar optimization adds an accuracy-dependent factor; O(log(1/epsilon_num)) is plausible under a regular bracket/conditioning assumption but is not asserted uniformly without that numerical regularity.

derived_results.claim: Under the source Theorem 5.2 assumptions, the exact/certified pair detector on the K-grid has the same high-probability late-change compute-delay curve r_K=(2K+1)/(2K-1) relative to the t-information I_t(P,Q).
derived_results.derivation: At t=T+D choose the deterministic grid lag g in [c_K D,D], c_K=(2K-1)/(2K+1); its trailing block is pure post-change. The source proof partitions theta-space into a compact inner neighborhood of the pre-change mean a and its exterior. On the inner set, uniform growth of the pure post block is g{I_t-2eta}; on the exterior, the prefix crossing block grows at order T by Lemma E.6. Taking D=r_K(1+epsilon)L/I_t gives g I_t>=(1+epsilon)L, so the same two-region proof shows the exact pair minimax exceeds A with probability tending to one. Thus tau_pair-T <= r_K(1+o_P(1))L/I_t. If K_A->infinity slowly, the leading high-probability factor approaches one with polylogarithmic active state.
derived_results.scope: This is a derived adaptation of the source high-probability theorem. The source Section 5.1 does not state a CADD result, and this checkpoint does not yet claim retry-amplified expected CADD for the studentized case because an explicit exponential finite-block miss bound for the predictive t e-process has not been proved here.

candidates_new.mechanism: For unknown Gaussian variance, keep one prefix universal-inference t e-process and a configurable recycled K-grid of post/recent starts; use certified two-e-process convex minimax scores as pathwise-lower evidence.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Source all-start computation is O(t log(1/epsilon_num)) per time and O(t) memory. Derived active start count is O(K log t), with high-probability delay factor r_K=(2K+1)/(2K-1) on the source t-information scale under Theorem 5.2 conditions; slowly increasing K approaches factor one.
candidates_new.scope: Novel synthesis/derivation. Exact false-alarm inheritance is strong; high-probability delay uses source asymptotics; expected CADD remains open.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Certified numerical lower bounds are mandatory; predictor state must be maintained exactly for retained starts; near-degenerate sample variance can worsen numerical conditioning; the finite-tail behavior needed for expected-delay retry amplification is not yet established.
candidates_new.confidence: high for pathwise validity and active-state reduction; medium-high for high-probability delay adaptation; open for CADD
